title: Requirement traceability block
description: Citations from a contracted operation to the requirements it exists to serve, and exclusions for operations that legitimately serve none. Operation-side only: requirement-side exclusions live in the capability's traceability-exclusions.yaml (see traceability-exclusions.schema.json), whose existence is also the reverse-enforcement opt-in (design D13). Written by the contract author; never inferred (design D1). Carried as `x-traceability` on an OpenAPI operation and as `traceability` on a CLI contract flag, positional, or command.

requirements.description: Requirement identifiers this operation serves, as `<capability>.<slug-of-heading>`. An identifier that resolves to no requirement fails the gate rather than being ignored: a citation nobody can follow is indistinguishable from no citation, and silently dropping it would let a reworded heading quietly un-trace an operation.

items.description: Capability prefix and heading slug, e.g. `agent-coordinator.lock-acquisition-is-exclusive`. The prefix is explicit so a cross-capability citation is visible as one.

excluded.description: This operation serves no requirement, deliberately. Mutually exclusive with `requirements` — an operation that cites and excludes at once is stating both that it has a purpose and that it has none.

reason.description: Why no requirement covers this operation. Written for a reviewer, not for the checker — the checker only asks that one exists. Say what would have to change for the exclusion to be removed, so the next reader can tell a real constraint from an old excuse. `Health probe; infrastructure rather than product surface` is a reason. `N/A` is not.

excluded.reason: Liveness probe for the container orchestrator. Infrastructure rather than product surface: no requirement describes it because no consumer calls it deliberately. Would need a requirement if the probe ever reported anything beyond process liveness.
